name: smart-field
title: Smart Field
description: An AI-proposed value for a single text field, shown with a confidence tier and its source before it becomes real data. The field's value never changes until the user explicitly accepts the proposal — clicking the trigger icon requests one via a consumer-supplied fetchProposal(currentValue, signal) function, which resolves to a SmartFieldProposal { value, confidence?: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high', provenance?: string } or null/undefined for no proposal. Once shown, the proposal renders in a panel below the field with Accept/Reject controls; accepting commits proposal.value into the field and shows a brief Undo affordance. Typing manually at any point (while loading or once a proposal is shown) cancels the in-flight request or dismisses the unaccepted proposal, since manual input always overrides an AI suggestion. Use for CRM/record enrichment, settings or profile fields, or any single structured field where AI has enough surrounding context to propose a value. Not for inline predictive continuation while typing (use ghost-input instead), multi-field or long-text diffing, or a consequential/risky action needing full review.

meta.engineeringNotes: Mirrors ghost-input's contract shape (value/onValueChange controlled-only, a fetchX behaviour injected by the consumer, an AbortSignal for cancellation) deliberately, so the AI tier reads as one consistent family rather than each component inventing its own pattern — the two differ only in what they return: a plain continuation string for ghost-input versus a structured { value, confidence, provenance } proposal here, because a complete replacement value needs that context attached and a continuation tail does not. Confidence rendering composes the shared `confidence-meter` primitive (extracted after Selection Actions needed the identical tiered indicator) rather than hand-rolling its own bars a second time — a three-tier enum (low/medium/high), not a raw number, because a fabricated percentage would claim precision the underlying model doesn't actually have, and because the system has no colour scale to spend on a red/yellow/green treatment anyway. autoPropose is opt-in and gated to empty fields only, adopted directly from CRM-enrichment research (Clay/HubSpot/Attio): confidence gates whether a proposal is allowed to overwrite existing data, so the safest default auto-behaviour is 'only ever fill a blank,' never 'silently reconsider what's already there.' Manual typing at any point cancels an in-flight fetch or dismisses a shown-but-unaccepted proposal, reusing ghost-input's staleness philosophy: a suggestion answering a question the field no longer asks is worse than no suggestion. The proposal panel animates open/closed via a CSS grid-template-rows trick (0fr to 1fr) rather than measuring and animating an explicit pixel height, which is the standard token-free way to animate a height that depends on variable content without a ResizeObserver.
meta.motionNotes: The proposal panel's height expansion and the field's colour tint both use --pd-duration-fast/--pd-ease-standard; the trigger's busy spinner and accept/reject colour changes use --pd-duration-instant, matching Button's press-feedback timing, because those are immediate state confirmations rather than content arriving. The proposed value itself never animates in character-by-character — the full value already exists the moment it's returned, so a typewriter reveal would misrepresent it as being generated live, the same reasoning ghost-input's plan already established. Confidence Meter (composed, not reimplemented here) has no motion of its own — under prefers-reduced-motion, the panel's grid-template-rows transition and the colour transitions are dropped via motion-reduce:transition-none, leaving the underlying state (panel present/absent, tint present/absent) fully legible without animation.

value.description: Current field value. SmartField is controlled — there is no uncontrolled mode.

triggerIcon.description: Icon shown in the trigger button. No bundled icon set — supply your own, size-4 recommended.

triggerLabel.description: Accessible label for the trigger button.

autoPropose.description:
Fetch a proposal automatically once mounted, if `value` is empty. Off by default —
fetching without an explicit ask contradicts the AI tier's "nothing happens
unannounced" posture, but some products (e.g. Notion's Custom Agent autofill) do
want this, so it's an opt-in rather than cut entirely.

proposeToken.description:
Changing this value requests a proposal. It exists so a parent can fill several
fields from one action — `AI Form Fill` bumps a single token and every field it
governs proposes at once — without this component giving up ownership of its own
proposal state. Ignored on first render, so mounting is never a request; use
`autoPropose` for that.

undoWindowMs.description: How long the Undo affordance stays visible after accepting, in ms.

UINode.description: A nested component: a name from this catalogue, and the props to give it.

props.description: That component's own props, matching its entry in this catalogue.

events.name: fetchProposal
events.description: Fetches a proposal for the current value. Return null/undefined for "no proposal".

events.name: onAcceptProposal
events.description: Fired after the user explicitly accepts a proposal.

docs: value/onValueChange are required — this is a controlled component only, matching ghost-input's contract. fetchProposal must resolve to the FULL proposed value (not a delta) plus optional confidence/provenance; return null/undefined for 'no proposal available' rather than throwing. triggerIcon is required with no bundled default — pass any size-4 SVG/icon element. autoPropose only fires once, on mount, and only when value is empty, so it can never silently overwrite existing data. Drops into <FieldControl> directly since id/aria-invalid/aria-describedby/ref all forward to the underlying <input>.
